task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-check of REQ-159's design after rework commit 31d5ccb.
acceptance_criteria: Section 5.1's fix confirmed present and correctly scoped (self-instance-only, :forbidden for anything else, no Repo lookup on rejection)
Control-flow and error-reason updates confirmed internally consistent
test/specs/REQ-159.md's updated tests confirmed to genuinely test the restriction
Full document re-skim confirms no other unstated authorization assumption exists
All 8 ACs still mapped, no regression elsewhere

checks.section_5_1_fix_present: PASS - the 'parent instance reading a known child's state' justification is fully removed. Section 5.1 is now titled 'Default scope: a script may only read its own instance's state (decided)' and states the script-supplied instance_id must equal execution_context.instance_id exactly, any other value (real or not) rejected uniformly with reason:"forbidden", no Repo lookup attempted for that value. It is explicitly framed as a decided design choice ('this is a default-scope decision ... not an open question') grounded in least-privilege reasoning and an honest citation check ('nothing in REQ-159's requirement text, its 8 acceptance criteria, LUA-11/LUA-13's text, decision 0014, or REQ-157's capability matrix asks for -- or even mentions -- a script reading any instance's state other than its own'), rather than inventing an ungrounded scenario as before.
checks.control_flow_error_enum_consistency: PASS - Section 5.2 step 2 checks argument well-formedness first (reason: invalid_id, ordered before the self-check so malformed input is never misreported as forbidden), step 3 explicitly compares instance_id (cast) against execution_context.instance_id and returns reason: forbidden with 'no Repo call is made' for this arm, step 4 only reaches Repo.get/3 when the two are equal. Section 5.3's four-value reason enum (no_execution_context, invalid_id, forbidden, not_found) matches this control flow exactly, and explicitly states forbidden is returned identically whether or not the other id exists, by design, so a script cannot use the error to probe which ids exist.
checks.test_spec_restriction_coverage: PASS - test/specs/REQ-159.md section 6 now has two explicit forbidden sub-cases under the same bullet, both asserting the identical "forbidden" outcome: (a) 'the other id belongs to a real InstanceProjection row in the same tenant schema (proves same-tenant cross-instance reads are rejected by default, not merely cross-tenant ones)' and (b) 'the other id is well-formed but names no row anywhere.' This directly satisfies the fix's own claim that a real sibling and a fabricated id are indistinguishable in the response. Section 5's valid-instance test also now requires the execution context's instance_id to equal the row's id, consistent with the self-scope restriction.
checks.full_document_reskim_no_other_hidden_ass: PASS - re-read section 0 (sources), 1 (scope), 2 (execution-context threading, closure-capture rationale, rejected alternatives (b)/(c)), 3 (LuaNumberMarshalling identity-function rules), 4 (read_variable - plain map lookup on execution_context.variables, never Repo), 6 (log - all three correlation fields sourced exclusively from execution_context, explicit 'never from the script's own arguments' statement), 7 (matrix/fold mechanics), 9 (cross-module deps), 10 (invariants), 11 (open questions OQ-1/OQ-2). No new unstated authorization assumption found: every place instance_id/prefix/trace_id/script_identity flows traces back to execution_context, itself sourced only from install/3's caller (trusted engine code, not the script), with no Lua-visible override path documented anywhere. OQ-1 (production wiring not yet built) and OQ-2 (log context size bound) remain properly flagged as open rather than silently resolved.
checks.acceptance_criteria_traceability: PASS - all 8 REQ-159 ACs (read directly from docs/requirements.yaml lines 8011-8019) still map in design section 8 to concrete design elements; AC3's row now explicitly notes the self-scope restriction and that any other instance id is uniformly forbidden.
checks.no_regression_elsewhere: PASS - cross-tenant prefix isolation unchanged (section 2.4, section 5.2 step 4 still uses execution_context.prefix exclusively), read_variable's map-only lookup unchanged (section 4.1, no Repo call), log's context-only sourcing unchanged (section 6.1/6.3), LuaNumberMarshalling identity-function rules unchanged and matching REQ-150 section 3, capability matrix rows (variable:read/instance:read/audit:log) unchanged (section 7.2/4.3/5.5/6.4).
checks.no_literal_elixir_code: PASS - grepped lib/letflow/design/req159-lua-host-api-read.md and test/specs/REQ-159.md for `fn `, `raise `, `case `, `cond `, `do:`, `->`; all hits are prose (e.g. 'raise shape', 'a raise propagating', 'still raise the', 'that would raise if') or code-fence @spec/@type declarations (signatures and type shapes only, not function bodies) -- no literal Elixir function implementation is present anywhere.
